visual_review: Direct original review shows a narrow dry stone-paved passage screened by irregular piled gray rocks, deep dark gaps and small perforations, an overhanging mass above the passage, trailing bare vines and pine branches. An upright inscribed stone panel and small visitor plaques sit beside the passage. Daylight lights the outer right rock faces while the left passage stays dark. The article identifies the south-entrance rockery; this supports the conceal-then-reveal composition and organic irregularity. It does not show the entire twelve-metre route or establish two bends, measured clearance, studio plaster, amber lanterns, fog or night lighting.

Rock and pine silhouettes partly screen the opening. The dark gate face and brighter lanterns beyond provide the requested dark-side moon-gate/fog composition.
